proposal: The Mandate recommends ending taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers: guidance that states may exclude them from Medicaid, a rule disqualifying elective-abortion providers from Medicaid, and congressional passage of a defunding bill. For Title X, it recommends rescinding the 2021 rule, reinstating the 2019 separation requirements, and expanding grantees beyond abortion providers.
remaining: A permanent statutory exclusion of abortion providers from Medicaid (the Mandate endorses the Protecting Life and Taxpayers Act); the one-year provision lapsed 2026-07-04 and no extension was found.
HHS guidance on state authority to exclude Planned Parenthood and a rule interpreting the Medicaid statute to disqualify elective-abortion providers (none found).

Expanding the Title X grantee pool beyond abortion providers (the April 2026 notices change grant priorities, but award outcomes were not found).
Decisions on the Section 1115 waiver requests from Idaho, South Carolina and Tennessee (no decision found).

status_summary: Section 71113 of Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) barred federal Medicaid payments to defined 'prohibited entities' (tax-exempt essential community providers mainly engaged in family planning that provide abortions outside narrow exceptions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid payments in fiscal year 2023, including affiliates) for services in the one-year period starting on enactment, a definition the D. Mass. court found reaches Planned Parenthood Federation members and their affiliates (it counted 46 covered providers, 44 of them Federation members or possible affiliates). In Planned Parenthood Federation of America v. Kennedy (D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11913, Judge Talwani) the court granted preliminary injunctions against enforcing section 71113 against Federation members on 2025-07-21 and 2025-07-28 on First Amendment, equal protection and bill of attainder grounds and denied a stay on 2025-08-29; a Wikipedia summary reports the First Circuit later allowed the ban to take effect (September 2025) and the plaintiffs dismissed their suit (January 2026). By its own terms the one-year period ended on 2026-07-04, and press reports say clinics resumed Medicaid billing for non-abortion services with no extension enacted before Congress recessed; extension efforts in 2026 (a Senate amendment in late April that failed, and calls for a third reconciliation bill) had not succeeded as of late July. On Title X, Sen. Josh Hawley's letter of 2026-04-02 says HHS released another year of funding under Title X grants approved under the prior administration, including to abortion providers such as Planned Parenthood, and that to his knowledge no rulemaking to reinstate the 2019 rule had begun. In addition, HHS's Office of Population Affairs lists a Fiscal Year 2027 Title X Services funding opportunity (PA-FPH-001, applications due 2027-01-11, up to $257 million for up to 90 awards, project periods up to five years) alongside research, infertility training and national training center opportunities; the Washington Examiner reports the April 2026 guidance and notices emphasize fertility-related conditions over contraception and restate that funds may not support programs where abortion is a method of family planning. The National Family Planning and Reproductive Health Association and a Pennsylvania grantee sued over the April changes in mid-June 2026, and Planned Parenthood Federation of America sued in the District of Columbia on 2026-07-28; no ruling was reported in either case. No rule reinstating the 2019 Title X regulation, no CMS guidance or rule on excluding abortion providers from Medicaid, and no action on the Idaho, South Carolina or Tennessee waiver requests were found.

timeline.event: Administration withholds Title X funds from all nine Planned Parenthood grantees (about $20.6 million) beginning late March to April 2025 (exact day not given, first of month used); some other grantees with Planned Parenthood clinics in their networks also receive withholding notices.

Public Law 119-21 is signed; section 71113 bars federal Medicaid payments to 'prohibited entities' for services furnished during the one-year period beginning on enactment (as described in the D. Mass. memorandum of 2025-07-28), defining such an entity as a 501(c)(3) essential community provider primarily engaged in family planning and related care that provides abortions outside narrow exceptions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid payments in fiscal year 2023, including affiliates. Press reports attribute the one-year limit to Senate reconciliation rules.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (via govinfo)

timeline.event: Judge Talwani (D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11913, Planned Parenthood Federation of America v. Kennedy) grants in part a preliminary injunction blocking enforcement of section 71113 against Federation members that will not provide abortions as of 2025-10-01 or whose fiscal year 2023 Medicaid payments did not exceed $800,000; on 2025-07-28 the court extends the injunction to all Federation members, finding plaintiffs likely to succeed on First Amendment, equal protection and bill of attainder claims. On 2025-08-29 the court denies the government's motion to stay the injunctions pending its First Circuit appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (via govinfo)

timeline.event: A Wikipedia summary reports that the First Circuit allowed the Medicaid funding ban to take effect after the district court's July 2025 injunction (September 2025; exact day not given, first of month used) and that Planned Parenthood filed a voluntary dismissal of its suit over the provision in January 2026; neither was confirmed against a court record.

HHS issues Title X guidance and a notice of funding opportunity for 2027 services that emphasizes fertility-related chronic conditions and restates the statutory bar on funds for programs where abortion is a method of family planning; the same day Sen. Josh Hawley's office publicizes an April 2 letter objecting to HHS releasing another year of funding on Title X grants approved under the prior administration and asking about a timeline for rulemaking to reinstate the 2019 Title X rule.

The one-year Medicaid prohibition expires; reports on 2026-07-04 and 2026-07-22 say the provision lapsed, clinics resumed Medicaid billing for non-abortion services, and no extension had passed, though anti-abortion groups urged including one in a third reconciliation bill.

Planned Parenthood Federation of America sues HHS officials in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia (No. 1:26-cv-02656) over the April 2026 Title X funding notices as modified in July, alleging violations of the Administrative Procedure Act and the Spending Clause. No ruling reported.

uncertainties: The text of section 71113 was not read directly in the public law (govinfo's page stops partway through the first title when fetched); its content comes from the D. Mass. memorandum of 2025-07-28 and order of 2025-08-29, read through fetch summaries, and the one-year period's end on 2026-07-04 follows from the enactment date and is reported by WAMC and OSV News. The Title X notices themselves were not read: the OPA page lists the FY2027 Title X Services opportunity and three others but shows no posting dates, priorities or July 2026 revisions, so the fertility emphasis and the abortion language rest on a Washington Examiner summary and a Bloomberg Law summary of the complaint. The 2025 First Circuit action and the January 2026 voluntary dismissal rest on a Wikipedia summary with month-only dates, and the First Circuit order was not located. The withheld 2025 Title X funds' later treatment is unclear (a senator's letter says HHS released another year of funding on previously approved grants). A Washington Examiner sidebar mentions a judge blocking other administration rules affecting Planned Parenthood, which was not investigated. No CMS guidance on state exclusion or Medicaid rulemaking was found in the Federal Register listing for HHS Title X terms or in the news reviewed. Checked on 2026-10-08: HHS's Office of Population Affairs funding opportunities page (read on this date; no posting dates shown) lists the Fiscal Year 2027 Title X Services opportunity (PA-FPH-001; applications due 2027-01-11; up to $257 million for up to 90 awards; project periods up to five years) and three other Title X opportunities (research grants, an infertility training center and a national training center); the page does not mention abortion or any July 2026 revision (opa.hhs.gov)
